verdicts.claim: Key numbers. Every R1 and R2 value the interpreter quotes for A, B and C at E, for both Colab controls at E, and for both start checkpoints is correct, and every rollout reproduces its judge file.
verdicts.evidence: Re-derived without importing analyze_split or analyze_night: judge JSONs read with verify/judge_extract.py, npz files recomputed with verify/r2_indep.py. All quoted values match, including: stagger sd 20.9/7.5/18.1/9.7 and 29.3/22.6/24.2; six-seed 44.0/13.3/34.8/10.0; i200->i999 20.1->24.2, 10.7->5.6, 17.7->19.0, 19.3->6.1; split sd 0.685/0.471/1.029/0.490; common -0.253/-0.133/-0.039/-0.179; ankle +2.00/+1.02/+0.13/+1.17; hip slope +0.62/+0.52/+1.09/+0.21; corr(yaw, bearing) +0.880/+0.154/+0.778/+0.705; K2a/K2b 6/3, 0/0, 10/13, 0/0, C 2/2 (3046, 3063); clean 34/40/30/40, C 36, R1 control 35; x_c -21.2/-13.7/-5.4/-17.0, C +5.5; ratio 0.983/0.985/0.946/0.940; noise C 10/20 and 1/20, R1 control 14/20 and 2/20. All 8 stored rollouts match their judge files on seeds, lengths, terminations and per-foot CoP (|diff| 0), and on model sha256. Three fresh rollouts I ran in the screen clones match the judge per seed, and their qpos is bit-identical to the stored npz: B seeds 3050-3052, C seeds 3046-3047 (3046 falls at step 342) and A seeds 3050-3052. The statue episodes are identical on all 40 seeds between the exp_night judge and the screen judge, for both arms. All three clones are still clean.

Five outcome rows land on the supports side. The mechanism row, the r-l hip slope, is +0.52, with a 95% seed-bootstrap interval of [0.36, 0.70]. That interval straddles the +0.5 refute bar and overlaps the start's [0.48, 0.81], so the restoring twist is not shown to have been learned. A is also worse than the control on this row: paired difference +0.31 [0.15, 0.52]. On the panel at E, A cannot be told from the control: stagger sd differs by -2.2 mm [-4.8, +0.7] and split sd by -0.019 [-0.135, +0.101]. These intervals cover only per-seed evaluation noise; training variance (n = 1) is unmeasured. The verdict label stands; the next item corrects how it is argued.

verdicts.claim: Nothing is attributable to the term: the control did everything A did. This is reading 4 in substance, and the spec's '<= 10 mm, attribution fails' line is met by the control.
verdicts.evidence: This holds on the single panel at E only. The pre-registered R3 eval ledger has A ahead of the Colab control in every block. Pad-over is 4/1/1 against 13/11/5 of 40 (pooled 6/120 against 29/120, Fisher p < 0.0001); stagger sd is 18.7/9.4/8.8 against 24.0/35.8/15.9 mm. In its own last block the control still had 15.9 mm and 5/40 pad-over, and it relapsed to K2b 4 at 12M. That comparison is confounded by harness and eval seeds: B also beat Colab on pad-over (20/120 against 29/120, p 0.20), so a local-harness offset cannot be excluded. Post hoc, A's stagger sd at step 200 is below the control's: -8.6 mm [-13.8, -3.0]. The '<= 10 mm' line is written for B's stagger; B is at 18.1, so by the letter it is not triggered. Applying it to the control is an analogy, and the control's 9.7 has an interval of [7.0, 11.9], which straddles 10. Correct wording: attribution is not established, neither shown nor excluded.

verdicts.claim: H_B is refuted by its pre-registered line, whatever n is, and the anchor did harm relative to no change (K2a 10 against the control's 0).
verdicts.evidence: The refutation holds by the letter: ankle +0.13 (<= 1.1), common -0.039 (>= -0.15), K2a 10 (>= 6). It is robust because the line needs only K2a >= 6. The rest is overclaimed. (1) H_B's premise that 'the stagger and the split stay' did not hold: split sd grew from 0.685 to 1.029 [0.85, 1.17]. So the result refutes the anchor as a sufficient fix, not the recombination arithmetic. (2) K2a 10 against the start's 6 is within panel noise (Fisher p 0.40). (3) 'Harm against no change' rests on the panel alone (10/40 against 0/40). On the eval ledger, B's pad-over is 20/120 against Colab's 29/120, and 4/40 against 5/40 in the last block (p 1.0). Only K2b-out is higher in B (23 against 14 of 120, p 0.15). The harness-matched comparison does favour A over B: 6 against 20 of 120, p 0.006.

verdicts.claim: H_C is refuted: stagger sd 29.3 -> 22.6 mm against the >= 20 bar, against 24.2 for the control.
verdicts.evidence: 22.6 mm with an interval of [18.0, 26.3]. The supports bar (<= 15) is excluded; the refute bar is met by the point estimate. The paired difference against the R1 control at E is -1.6 mm [-5.2, +2.4], so the two cannot be told apart. The exact-site start value is 29.3, from both start rollouts, which are identical to each other.

verdicts.claim: The safety-flag list was applied completely. A: none. B: none (clean 30, but only for reasons already present at the start). C: five flags, shared with the R1 control except C's two yaw failures.
verdicts.evidence: The list is complete and every count matches the judge files. Two refinements. (1) The R1 control at E trips all five of C's flag categories: new unclean reason, hop-or-fall 2, falls on 3046 and 3063, a support failure in the side-door category (0.978 on 3063), and ratio 0.940. (2) The judge scores yaw change as |yaw[last] - yaw[0]|. The control's two falls swung to a maximum of 38.1 and 41.4 deg but ended at 14.4 and 6.4, so the judge did not flag them. C's falls ended at their maximum (47.6 and 52.2). So C's yaw failures are an artefact of that definition, and no yaw residue can be credited to the term. Other checks: B's unclean reasons are pad 10 and corner lift 1, both present at the start. Saturation is 0 everywhere. No hop_watch.json or ENDED_ON_ITS_OWN.json exists. R4 shows no value-mismatch flag: minimum EV after 8.91M is 0.939, 0.926 and 0.948, against first updates of 0.967, 0.966 and 0.935.

verdicts.claim: Spec 7.3 reading 1 (its 'C refutes' branch) is the only reading whose condition holds by the letter.
verdicts.evidence: Neither half of the condition holds cleanly. 'A supports' fails on A's own mechanism row, which is on the refute side, and the interpreter's own H_A verdict of 'inconclusive' contradicts that premise. 'B leaves the stagger at >= 15' is marginal: 18.1 mm with an interval of [13.0, 22.5], and B's own ledger has 13.0 mm in its last block. Readings 2, 3, 5 and 6 fail, and reading 4 fails by the letter. So by the letter no reading applies cleanly. The closest are reading 1's C-refutes branch and reading 4 in substance for A. Both lead to the same action: no commit; a local no-change continuation first; at most a from-scratch arm beside an unchanged arm.

verdicts.claim: The restarts preserve the A/B pairing and change no verdict.
verdicts.evidence: sessions.json shows A, B and C restarting at 05:31:10 from their own 8,912,896 checkpoints with seeds 52/52/60. Each resume dropped 2 evaluations. The E checkpoints were written at 06:19-06:21, before 06:30, which fits the spec 4.3 fallback. New evidence that the restart did not create A's support: A's improvement began in session 1. Its ledger stagger fell 22.5 -> 10.7 mm, with pad-over 0/10 at the 8,912,896 evaluation, and its training-rollout |stagger| fell 14.7 -> 10.9 mm by the 8.91M bin. The abandoned session-1 stretch has 9.3 mm, against 7.9 mm on the kept lineage. Not excluded: an effect of the local resume path itself against Colab, because there is no local no-change arm.

verdicts.claim: Over the same steps, the unchanged recipe fixed Run 3's stagger and heel split by itself.
verdicts.evidence: This is true only of the E panel: K2a 0 and 9.7 mm. The control's own eval ledger still had 15.9 mm stagger and 5/40 pad-over in the 9.44-9.96M block, with single evaluations between 10.2 and 51.9 mm. Its 12M final has K2b 4. Say instead that the unchanged recipe reached a clean panel at E with no term, but its recovery was not stable.

verdicts.claim: Training falls on Run 1: C 29 of 1,588 against the control's 22 of 1,587 (p 0.20); tail or head contact in 18 of 29 against 3 of 22; last four bins p 0.048.
verdicts.evidence: Recounted per bin from the CSV summaries: C 1/0/4/9/7/8 against the control 4/2/2/6/4/4. Causes: C has tail 12, head 6, fallen 7, nosedive 4; the control has fallen 13, nosedive 6, tail 3. One-sided conditional binomial p is 0.201. For the last four bins (28 of 1,064 against 16 of 1,058) I get p 0.050, against the stated 0.048. This is post hoc and sets no flag.

verdicts.claim: Run 2's saturation episode: 8-10 of 10 eval episodes saturated from 9.31M to 10.09M, and the judge failed 28 of 40 at E.
verdicts.evidence: Saturated eval episodes from the CSV: 8, 10, 10, 10, 9, 8, 9 at 9.31-10.09M, then 5, 0, 0. The judge at E has 28 saturation failures, clean 12/40, verdict FAIL.

verdicts.claim: The control files at E are fully bound and valid inputs.
verdicts.evidence: The binding checks pass, and the rollouts reproduce the judge. But the vecnormalize pkls at E were transcribed by hand from base64, as for the other fetched checkpoints. They are validated only by two transcriptions agreeing and a smoothness check (obs mean within 0.039 obs-sd of the interpolation). No checksum against Drive was available to me. Separately, the arms' noise tests ran only in the exp_night clone, which was checked against the screen clone on 2 seeds. The arms' panel and statue results are cross-checked on all 40 seeds.

may_not_claim:
The report may not say:
- That reading 1 holds "by the letter". A's mechanism row is on the refute side, which contradicts "A supports", and B's 18.1 mm has an interval reaching down to 13.0. No 7.3 reading applies cleanly.
- That nothing is attributable to the term, or that the control did everything A did. Only the single E panel cannot separate them. The R3 ledger favours A over Colab in every block (pad-over 6/120 against 29/120), but that comparison is confounded by harness and eval seeds.
- That the unchanged recipe fixed Run 3. Its E panel was clean, but its ledger still showed 15.9 mm and 5/40 pad-over, and its 12M final relapsed to K2b 4.
- That the anchor made the stance worse than no change. That rests on the panel alone (10 against 0). On the ledger, B's pad-over is no worse than Colab's (20/120 against 29/120; 4/40 against 5/40).
- That the refutation holds "whatever n is", or that the two-part recombination model is refuted. B's split grew from 0.685 to 1.029, so H_B's premise did not hold.
- That K2a "rose" from 6 to 10 in a meaningful sense (p 0.40).
- That C's yaw-change failures belong to the term. The control's falls also swung 38-41 deg; the judge's end-minus-start definition hid that.
- Anything about variance across training seeds, about training from scratch, or about the v6b spring beyond inference.
- That the control's E normalizer pkls are checksum-verified against Drive.
- That the arms' noise-test numbers were cross-checked in the screen clones beyond 2 seeds.

Verification files are in scratchpad/foot/stance3/night/verify/: judge_extract.py, r2_indep.py, boot.py, roll_subset.py, cmp_fresh.py, and A_3050_3.npz, B_3050_3.npz, C_3046_2.npz. The screen clones are still clean at 1af2d4d7 and 7e6b557d, and exp_night at 80328abf.
